clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of fever, progressive headache, weakness, and paresthesias in both legs, along with slight neck stiffness. Lumbar puncture revealed cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with moderate pleocytosis (140 leucocytes/μL) and mononuclear cell dominance, consistent with viral meningoencephalitis. The known final diagnosis is Tickborne encephalitis virus (TBEV) infection.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms suggestive of meningoencephalitis, including 1-week fever, progressive headache, weakness in both legs, paresthesias in both legs, and slight neck stiffness.
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed moderate pleocytosis (140 leucocytes/μL) with a mononuclear cell dominance, consistent with viral central nervous system infection.

remaining_uncertainties: Direct laboratory confirmation of Tickborne encephalitis virus (TBEV) infection (e.g., positive TBEV IgM/IgG in CSF/serum or PCR) was not provided in the reports.
Epidemiological risk factors such as recent tick bites, outdoor activities, or travel to endemic areas for tickborne diseases were not reported.
